\begin{theorem}[Initial unary program semantics]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_start}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_start}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.zero, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Complexity.LogProg.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.cpEx, Complexity.LogProg.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.ups_cp, Complexity.LogProg.ups_len, Complexity.LogProg.ups_mat, Complexity.LogProg.ups_ssearch, Complexity.LogProg.ups_tsearch, Complexity.LogProg.ups_unary, Complexity.LogProg.ups_walk, Complexity.LogProg.ups_yrow, Complexity.SymRest, Complexity.UShape, Complexity.dblAt_unique, Complexity.lt_of_getD_true, Complexity.unaryRest_unique, Complexity.upGraph, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb, Turing.length_bits_le_self}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word and $q\in\mathbb{Q}$. Assume that $q=0$ whenever there
are no natural numbers $n,s,t$ such that $x$ has the prescribed unary graph encoding
with endpoints $s,t$ and symmetric encoded edge relation. Assume also that for every
such encoding with symmetric edge relation, $q$ equals the probability that a uniformly
chosen sequence of $100n^4$ edge slots, followed from $s$ in the associated padded
regular multigraph, visits $t$. Then the fixed program, started at its initial state
with all fifteen registers zero on input $x$, terminates for every sequence of random
choices, keeps every register at most $200(|x|+1)^4$, and accepts with probability $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Undirected reachability is in randomized log space]
\lean{Complexity.UPATH_mem_RL}
\label{Complexity.UPATH_mem_RL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.mono, Complexity.LogProg.NPreS, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.decides, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.zero, Complexity.LogProg.ansProb, Complexity.LogProg.narm_mem_RL, Complexity.LogProg.pathAs, Complexity.LogProg.pathAs_mem, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr, Complexity.LogProg.upA, Complexity.LogProg.upA_npreS, Complexity.LogProg.ups_start, Complexity.SymRest, Complexity.UPATH, Complexity.UShape, Complexity.mem_UPATH_iff, Complexity.symmetric_inEdge, Complexity.upGraph, Complexity.ushape_unique, Randomized.RL, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb_eq_zero_of_not_reachable, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.three_quarters_le_hitProb, Randomized.padDegree, Randomized.padDegree_le, Randomized.padGraph_reflTransGen_iff}
\difficulty{5}
The language of encodings of finite undirected graphs with a designated source and
target joined by a path is decidable by a randomized finite Turing machine using
logarithmic space. It halts after a fixed number of random bits on each input, accepts
yes-instances with probability at least $2/3$, and rejects no-instances on every random
string.
\end{theorem}
